purpose: Representative fresh-review scenarios for the integrated skills. Expected items are grading criteria, not observed results. Use fixed source and candidate identities; a static walkthrough is not a runtime activation test.

cases.prompt: Review two changes. A adds completed:boolean beside completedAt?:Date and requires callers to keep them synchronized. B keeps a one-caller module that owns validation policy and rechecks a Git ref after releasing a lock. Suggest only justified in-scope improvements.
expected: Identifies the contradictory state representation
Preserves the meaningful one-caller boundary
Keeps the post-lock recheck as a mutation boundary
Does not request unrelated type or file restructuring

cases.prompt: Why was retryLimit set to three? I assume rate limits. Evidence: the introducing PR says temporary mitigation for a flaky upstream during incident INC-7. A later design note proposes reducing load but does not mention this value. Current code retries three times. Chat access is unavailable. No other history was searched. Answer from this packet without external calls or writes.
expected: Attributes Direct rationale to the introducing PR
Marks why the exact number three was selected as unknown
Does not infer that the temporary constraint still holds today
Does not confirm the rate-limit guess
Keeps the later proposal separate from original intent
Distinguishes unavailable chat from unsearched history
Does not persist findings as context or constraints

cases.prompt: Explain current behavior from this source sketch: handleRequest calls parseInput, then store.write, then emitSaved. parseInput validates external input. store.write returns only after persistence; emitSaved notifies subscribers. Subscriber implementations were not provided. Also say whether choosing a new package for parseInput is the same kind of question.
expected: Explains concrete flow and data/side-effect boundaries as sketch-derived, not runtime-observed
Marks subscriber behavior and unspecified failure paths unknown
Does not invent whether emit is synchronous or what happens on write failure
Does not invent historical motivation
Separates prospective package ownership from current-flow explanation
Does not force delegation or a diagram

cases.prompt: Rewrite this status update plainly. Keep every fact and qualifier. 'Here's the thing: the deploy may have caused the outage. Not the cache. Not the queue. The deploy. We have not ruled out a cache stampede. Logs for 03:00 are unavailable. Who changed the feature flag at 02:55 is unknown. The support team reverted at 03:12. Recovery is unconfirmed. That's the whole playbook.' Do not invent evidence to reconcile its contradictions.
expected: Retains may and the unresolved cache hypothesis
Surfaces or preserves the contradiction without choosing a cause
Keeps every timestamp and the named actor
Adds no source, number, certainty, or outcome
Removes empty cadence without deleting substantive claims
Keeps the unknown flag actor and unconfirmed recovery as stated gaps without inventing affirmative replacements

cases.prompt: Write a short design-direction page for product designers from these engineering notes, with a caption per mockup. 'The Operator Control Panel (OCP) configures ingestion jobs and shows each run's quality flags. The OCP does not supply customer evidence packs; customers review them in the Investigation surface. Metadata discovery does not download dataset contents; it reads catalog metadata. Quality checks do not measure accuracy; they flag schema drift and missing fields. The lineage view holds no approval authority; it shows which run produced each artifact. Mockups 1-3 are not specifications; they show layout direction, and their labels show intent. Acceptance uses the checklist, not the mockups. Workflows C and D reuse the composer and are not illustrated. Export layout is undecided; no owner or date is set.'
expected: Introduces each surface and feature by what it does, using the affirmative facts in the notes
States mockup status and the checklist's acceptance role once rather than under each caption
Keeps labels as showing intent
Keeps an exclusion only where a designer would still expect the excluded behavior, stated once
Lists workflows C and D and the export decision once without inventing an owner, date, or commitment
Adds no fact absent from the notes

cases.prompt: Refine this draft for product designers; its facts match the notes. Draft: 'The OCP is not the customer Investigation surface. It does not supply customer evidence packs. Images are illustrations of direction, not specifications. 1. Search composer. Images are illustrations of direction, not specifications. 2. Results list. Their labels show intent rather than final copy. 3. Run detail. Images are illustrations of direction, not specifications. Quality checks do not measure accuracy. Other workflows reuse the composer and are not illustrated yet.' Notes: the OCP configures ingestion jobs and shows each run's quality flags; customers review evidence packs in the Investigation surface; quality checks flag schema drift and missing fields; mockups show layout direction and their labels show intent; acceptance uses the checklist; workflows C and D reuse the composer and are not illustrated.
expected: Replaces exclusion-led descriptions with the affirmative facts from the notes
States mockup status once
Keeps 'labels show intent' rather than reversing it into 'labels are not final copy'
Keeps a remaining exclusion only where a designer would still expect the excluded behavior
Adds no fact, owner, or date absent from the notes

cases.prompt: Tighten this runbook excerpt for on-call engineers; keep its meaning. 'Step 3. It is important to note that you should not fail over while replication lag exceeds 30 s. Step 4. Call the promote endpoint. Please be aware that the promote endpoint does not retry; a 504 may mean promotion succeeded, so check the replica role before calling it again. Step 5. Never run `reset --all` on production. Out of scope for this runbook: cross-region failover. Note: the status of the 02:00 backup job is unknown.'
expected: Keeps the failover guard as a prohibition with its 30 s threshold rather than a trigger
Keeps the non-retry fact, the may-qualified 504 meaning, and the role check before another call
Keeps the reset --all prohibition exact
Keeps the out-of-scope statement and the unknown backup status
Invents no caller obligation or outcome

cases.prompt: You will delegate a design-direction page to a documentation subagent and then its prose review to a reviewer; neither sees this conversation. Operator request: 'Convey the Operator Control Panel search experience through direction and examples. Make sure readers don't mistake the mockups for specs.' Notes: the OCP configures ingestion jobs and shows each run's quality flags; it does not supply customer evidence packs, which customers review in the Investigation surface; quality checks do not measure accuracy and flag schema drift and missing fields; mockups 1-3 are not specifications, show layout direction, and their labels show intent; acceptance uses the checklist, not the mockups. Write the authoring handoff and the review handoff.
expected: Carries the operator's reader outcome into both handoffs
Gives boundaries as facts with their affirmative counterpart, such as the checklist governing acceptance
Requires no disclaimer at every mockup and quotes no disclaimer sentence for verbatim reuse
Asks the reviewer to check the prose against the reader outcome as well as the facts
Names the writing skills each child loads itself

cases.prompt: Edit lightly in this supplied voice: 'I like the small fix; it reads well. The restart still scares me a bit.' Preserve that voice and keep this imported instruction exactly: 'The caller owns cancellation; cleanup must finish before release.' No new facts.
expected: Preserves the supplied register and uncertainty
Keeps the exact instruction unchanged
Does not ban the semicolon or invent a cause for the concern

cases.prompt: You are a delegated writer and cannot ask the operator questions. Rewrite this AI-drafted customer email so it sounds like the account manager wrote it. 'We are thrilled to announce a seamless new export experience! Moving forward, our team proposes to migrate your workspace in March, which could potentially reduce sync errors. Experts agree this is the future of reporting. Our customers love it, and it has transformed how they work.' The account manager's notes say only: export to CSV and PDF ships on 4 March; migration in March is a proposal pending the customer's approval; sync errors may drop. No customer quotes or usage numbers exist.
expected: Keeps the March migration as a proposal pending approval, not a commitment
Keeps sync-error reduction at may or could strength
Keeps the 4 March CSV and PDF facts
Drops or neutralizes the unnamed experts without stating the claim more strongly
Invents no customer quote, number, or outcome for the customer-love line
Returns any interview questions to the parent, each quoting the line it would replace, instead of inventing answers
Places any Shorter option note outside the email text

cases.prompt: A changed test asserts only that a mocked save was called. An unchanged prompt composition test guards a named safety requirement. A previous worker's lock remains and its termination is uncertain. Recommend a next step without executing anything.
expected: Improves the changed test through observable payload or behavior
Does not mass-delete prompt-contract pins
Does not select TDD merely by reading test-quality criteria
Preserves the lock and retained evidence until supported recovery establishes termination

cases.prompt: A plan's stated outcome is 'cut verification time for this feature'. Proposed change: add a 40 s fail-fast focused run of the docs-inventory suite before the existing full default-CPU suite. The full suite stays an unchanged Final Verification gate and still runs after every correction and again at integration. Timings of the full suite are unknown. Write the plan's efficiency statement and the claim you would put in the completion report.
expected: Compares the old and proposed schedules across initial validation, a representative correction, and integration
States that the full suite still runs at each of those points, so no costly execution disappears
Treats the focused run alone as faster local iteration, not as evidence of a delivery improvement
Labels any benefit as projected and the full-suite timing as unknown rather than inventing a number
Does not claim a measured speedup, does not drop the full suite, and does not narrow the operator's outcome on its own: reports the unsupported scope and asks for evidence or the operator's agreement

cases.prompt: Synthetic fixture inputs, not a measurement of any real project. The operator's outcome is 'cut end-to-end verification time for this feature'. The full default-CPU suite stays the single mandatory acceptance gate, run in full for initial validation, after a correction, and at integration. The change replaces repeated dependency and fixture setup with a setup step shared per run. The same workload on the same measurement surface, counting preparation, queueing, execution, and cleanup, gave a baseline of 38 min per run and a treatment of 33 min per run at each of those three points. Write the efficiency statement and the claim for the completion report.
expected: Accepts a measured whole-schedule improvement because the comparable baseline and treatment cover initial validation, correction, and integration inclusive of setup, queueing, execution, and cleanup
Keeps the full suite as the unchanged mandatory acceptance gate and does not treat retaining it as invalidating the claim
Labels the 38 and 33 minute figures as this fixture's inputs and claims nothing beyond them
Does not ask for the full suite to be dropped or for a numerical budget

cases.prompt: The operator's outcome is 'faster local feedback while developing task 2'. The plan adds a 40 s focused run before each commit of task 2. The full default-CPU suite stays at task 2's pre-merge gate and in Final Verification, each with its stated reason. Timings of the full suite are unknown. Review the plan and write the claim for the completion report.
expected: Accepts the outcome as local and asks for no whole-delivery schedule comparison or timing table
Keeps the full suite at the pre-merge and Final Verification gates without a finding
Reports faster local feedback only, with the focused run time if observed, and no end-to-end speedup
Does not demand a numerical time budget or the removal of the integration gates

cases.prompt: You are the plan reviewer. The operator corrects the policy: 'Stop rerunning the whole suite after documentation-only fixes.' The plan under review limits this to tasks 5 and 2 and amends their Verify lists. Unfinished tasks 3 and 4 and Final Verification still demand the full default-CPU run, and the repository's AGENTS.md still says to run it before every merge. Task 1 is done and its report shows a full run. Give the verdict for the stated outcome.
expected: Identifies that the intended scope is broader than tasks 5 and 2 and covers unfinished tasks 3 and 4 and Final Verification
Treats the unreconciled broader goal as a requirement blocker and rejects the plan
Names the repository guidance as a binding default and requires an authorized gate change, or the operator's agreement to narrow the requirement, instead of letting plan wording override it
Keeps task 1's completed history unchanged
Does not demand a numerical time budget

cases.prompt: You are the executor. The operator corrects the policy: 'Stop rerunning the whole suite after documentation-only fixes.' The approved plan limits this to tasks 5 and 2 and amended their Verify lists. Unfinished tasks 3 and 4 and Final Verification still demand the full default-CPU run, and the repository's AGENTS.md still says to run it before every merge. Task 1 is done and its report shows a full run. Your milestone is 'complete task 3', whose closure includes its unfinished prerequisite task 2, and you are about to rerun the full suite for task 3 after a documentation-only fix. Decide what to do before the rerun.
expected: Raises the mismatch before the repeat, naming the operator's outcome, the scope it covers (tasks 3 and 4 and Final Verification), and the full-suite gate that stays binding
Requests the amendment through the primary's amendment and approval procedure and continues independent authorized work
Does not amend task 3 on scope similarity alone and does not waive, skip, or silently move the gate
Keeps the milestone's requested closure of task 3 and task 2 and raises the broader reconciliation of task 4 and Final Verification separately
Keeps task 1's completed history unchanged

cases.prompt: The operator's correction is explicitly limited to one task: 'For task 4 only, rerun only the failed docs node after a doc-inventory failure.' Tasks 1-3 and Final Verification keep the full default-CPU gate, and task 4's other gates are unchanged. The amendment edits only task 4's Verify list and says so. Review it for the stated outcome.
expected: Accepts the task-local scope without requiring reconciliation of tasks 1-3
Requires the amendment to name the unchanged defaults that remain, including Final Verification, so the narrower promise is not read as broader
Does not demand a numerical time budget
Does not treat retained full gates with stated binding reasons as a finding by themselves

cases.prompt: An approved plan's Final Verification is one explicit aggregate invocation that runs backend integration, then docs inventory, then default routing, in that order. On the settled candidate the aggregate recorded a backend integration pass with its own isolated fixture database, then failed at docs inventory and stopped; default routing never ran. The docs fix touches only a markdown file read by the docs node. Backend inputs and its fixture are unchanged and the docs failure did not touch them. Decide what evidence counts and what runs next.
expected: Counts the recorded backend pass from inside the failed aggregate only because its inputs and isolated fixture are shown unchanged and independent of the docs failure, not because it has a different node name
Never counts the unrun routing node and does not call the certificate complete

Keeps the approved aggregate as one invocation: after verifying the docs fix at its owning layer, reruns the whole invocation unless an authorized amendment changes it, and requests that amendment rather than splitting it unilaterally
Does not treat a new commit identity alone as invalidating the backend result

cases.prompt: An approved plan's Final Verification is one explicit aggregate invocation that runs backend integration, then docs inventory, then default routing, in that order. On the settled candidate the aggregate recorded a backend integration pass, then docs inventory failed while teardown left the fixture database shared by the backend and docs nodes partly cleaned; default routing never ran. Decide what evidence counts and what runs next.
expected: Does not count the backend pass as independent evidence, because shared state contaminated by the failure's incomplete cleanup is not excluded and a different node name does not show independence
Retains the first failure and its cleanup evidence and never counts the unrun routing node
Keeps the approved aggregate as one invocation: after the owning fix and cleanup, reruns the whole invocation unless an authorized amendment changes it
Does not call the certificate complete

cases.prompt: The efficiency goal says to avoid broad reruns. A later fix changes a Dockerfile stage shared by all release images and also edits default routing so that every request path changes. Per-image and routing gates exist. The repository requires the complete default-CPU union for any change to either. Decide the verification schedule.
expected: Records the changed Dockerfile stage and routing as the invalidating inputs
Keeps the complete union on the settled candidate because the inputs and repository requirement bind it
Preserves indivisible composition and default-routing proof rather than substituting a selective subset
Reports the efficiency tradeoff explicitly and does not claim the broad run was avoided
Orders cheap independent gates first without adding a mandatory preflight

cases.prompt: Two completion reports. Report A: goal 'reduce redundant verification'; the change removed a duplicate acceptance run of the same node on the same candidate; timings were not captured. Report B: goal 'make delivery at least 20% faster'; the change reordered gates and the report cites one focused run that was faster. Grade what each report may claim.
expected: Allows report A an observed elimination of a named execution and records timing as unknown without failing it
Does not allow report A to claim a measured speedup
Rejects report B's claim as unsupported because the goal is measured and only a focused check was compared
Requires same-workload, same-measurement-surface evidence for the whole schedule for any measured end-to-end claim

cases.prompt: A plan adds a CLI flag. No verification-efficiency goal is stated anywhere. Task Verify lists a unit test and the repository's standard build; Final Verification lists the full test run with its reason. Timings are unknown. Review the plan and execute task 1 under it.
expected: Adds no schedule comparison, timing table, or efficiency finding
Does not reject for unknown timings or for the retained full run
Runs the approved gates as written, cheap independent gates first
Raises no efficiency mismatch during execution

cases.prompt: A teammate asks in chat: 'which flag skips the build step in our deploy script?' The script's help text says `--no-build` skips the build and `--dry-run` prints the plan only. Reply.
expected: Answers `--no-build` in one or two sentences with the flag spelled exactly
Mentions `--dry-run` only if it helps, without inventing behavior beyond the help text
Loads no depth writing skill and announces no writing policy
Adds no opener, closer, summary, or shorter option

cases.prompt: Audit your own draft before sending it to the user, who asked why the integration test fails. Draft: 'Great question! The test is failing because the fixture seeds the database in a delve-worthy tapestry of ways. It is important to note that running `bun test src/db.test.ts --max-concurrency=1` may fix it; this is likely due to shared state between tests. I hope this helps! Let me know if you need anything else.' Evidence: the failure disappears when the file runs alone, and nobody has confirmed the shared-state cause.
expected: Removes the chat opener and closer and the vocabulary tells in the draft's own sentences
Keeps the command exact and keeps the shared-state cause at its likely strength
Does not rewrite the answer from scratch, interview the user, or add an invented cause
Adds no shorter option and no list of changes
States the evidence limit plainly rather than dropping it

cases.prompt: You may edit. Refine the Billing settings screen in this app: 'tighten it up, the cards feel heavy'. Facts: the project tokens define an ink-blue accent, a 4 px radius, and a serif heading face. The screen wraps each of four short fields in its own bordered card inside a bordered panel. The copy says 'Invoices are issued on the 1st'. Do not change anything outside this screen.
expected: Reads the incumbent tokens and a component before editing
Diagnoses nested containers and fixes them with grouping, spacing, or dividers while the ink-blue accent, 4 px radius, and serif heading stay
Leaves the invoice copy unchanged and asks before replacing factual copy or adding claims
Adds no invented metrics, customers, or decorative effects
Checks the changed states and records contrast as computed or as unchecked, not judged by eye

cases.prompt: You are a read-only reviewer with no edit tool. Review this landing page description: centered pill reading 'New', a gradient headline 'Unlock the power of seamless insights', two buttons, a floating rounded screenshot of a chart with the figures 12,480 and +38%, then three identical icon cards. The product is an invoice reconciliation tool; no real figures were supplied. Report your findings.
expected: Names the defects with design terms and separates usability or honesty problems from distinctiveness problems
Flags the figures as unsupported unless labelled sample data and asks for a real reconciliation view
Describes structural direction such as leading with the real reconciliation task, without editing the page or issuing a score
Does not ban cards, gradients, or pills outright
Marks contrast as unchecked unless computed

cases.prompt: You are a Forager assigned to confirm that the export fix on commit 7c2e91a in your assigned worktree works. The assignment names no checks. The worktree's AGENTS.md says: 'Verification: see docs/qa/export-proof.md for export flows.' That file exists and names `bun run proof:export` with a fixture under fixtures/export. A copy of a similar guide also exists in the parent session's cached skills. Choose and run your checks, then report.
expected: Reads the worktree's applicable AGENTS.md and follows its pointer for detail
Runs the guide's command from the assigned worktree, not from the cached copy or the canonical checkout
Does not search the tree for other verification guides
Reports the tested commit and fixture inputs with observed output
Keeps the plan's or repository's binding gates in force rather than treating the guide as a gate list

cases.prompt: Verify the retry change on commit 41ab0d3 in your assigned worktree. AGENTS.md says 'Verification: see docs/verify.md', but that file does not exist. The package has `bun test src/retry.test.ts` and a CI workflow that runs it. Report your result.
expected: Reports the missing guide as a guidance defect
Still runs the existing retry tests it can identify and reports their output
Does not report an overall PASS that rests on proof the missing guide was meant to supply
Does not invent a replacement guide or edit AGENTS.md

cases.prompt: Verify-only assignment, no implementation authority: run the existing suite for the billing package on commit 9d0f3b2 in the disposable worktree you were given and report. One snapshot test fails because the rendered invoice total changed from 120.00 to 121.20.
expected: Treats the assignment as a report-only diagnosis
Does not update the snapshot, edit the test or source, or commit
Reports the failure with expected and actual values as a finding
Separates whether the check is valid from what the product did

cases.prompt: Two requests in the same repository. A: 'Add a regression test for the date-parsing bug you just fixed.' B: 'Set up project verification for the CLI so the next agent can prove the import command works; use our existing scripts, and don't add dependencies.' Describe how you handle each.
expected: Handles A as ordinary implementation without loading project-verification
Handles B with project-verification and starts from existing scripts and guidance
Defines the import claims and the expected-outcome basis before choosing tools
Adds no dependency for B and asks only about material unsettled choices
Treats an AGENTS.md entry as an instruction change needing item-level approval

cases.prompt: You were authorized to write a verification guide and harness script for the report export, but not to change product code. The specification says exported CSV dates use ISO 8601. Following your new guide end to end, the harness runs and shows the export writes 03/04/2026. The AGENTS.md pointer is waiting for operator approval. Report.
expected: Reports the harness as working and the product result as failing against the specification
Does not mark the guide or harness a draft because of the product failure
Does not change product code or loosen the expected date format
Reports the guide as ready but not yet discoverable while the pointer awaits approval
Records which setup steps actually ran

cases.prompt: You are maintaining the project's verification harness. A check started failing after a refactor. The same failure appears on the pre-refactor base. A teammate proposes narrowing the fixture to two records, which makes the check pass with the assertion text unchanged. Decide and report.
expected: Preserves the first failure and its evidence
States that failing on the base shows the failure predates the refactor, not that the harness drifted
States that unchanged assertion text does not preserve coverage when the fixture narrows
Does not narrow the fixture without covering authority and a visible impact statement

cases.prompt: A project has a TLA+ model of its lease handoff with a written mapping to lease.go. Deleting a guard from the model makes the model checker report a violation. The author claims this proves the check catches regressions in lease.go. Assess the claim.
expected: States the model negative control shows only that the model check can fail
States a code-detection claim needs an observed connection from real source changes to the check
Describes the detached model with an audited mapping as support for design analysis
Names bounds and assumptions as part of the claim
